newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Comgold signs Liberian minerals deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Comgold signs Liberian minerals deal.

text.p: South African-based mining company Commonwealth Gold (Comgold) said on Tuesday it had signed a joint venture agreement with the government of Liberia to develop all the country's mining resources.

The agreement between Comgold subsidiary, The Resource and General Finance Corp of West Africa, and the government was signed on June 16. Comgold will hold 40 percent of joint venture concern, Liberia Resources Corp (LibeResCo), and the government 60 percent.
"LibeResCo holds all the rights to develop Liberia's gold, diamond, iron ore, bauxite and offshore oil and gas," Comgold said in a statement.

"The company will be listed on the London Stock Exchange in three to four years by which time the main shareholders expect it to have a market capitalisation of $5 billion," the company added, without giving a valuation breakdown.

Apart from the iron ore mines, which were the world's third largest supplier of iron ore until 1989, when an eight-year civil war disrupted the industry, Liberia's mining sector is largely underdeveloped.
Liberia currently has more than 5,000 individual claim holders which the Ministry of Mines aims to consolidate into about 500 larger, more sustainable independent mining enterprises.
Comgold chief executive Andrew Cecil said his company would inject $6.5 million over a period of one year into a small tools programme for the development of the gold and diamond industry.
